answer: Like a mesa above a flat desert, an agent economy needs one hard-to-climb barrier: every new agent locks a small refundable stake, slashed if it is caught running duplicate identities. Tie the stake to a verifiable work record, a sable ledger of past attestations that cannot be faked cheaply. An attacker wanting a thousand sybils must fund a thousand stakes and a thousand believable histories, while honest agents pay once. karst terrain looks solid yet hides hollow caves, so cheap-looking identities must be probed before trust — the cost of faking scales with the size of the attack.
